claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the documented record is sufficient to defend rejecting the vendor because admissible due-diligence evidence showed a material unresolved risk, framed as unresolved storage-control questions plus documented process-maturity and quality-execution concerns, rather than a confirmed control failure.
specific_concerns: The policy threshold is 'material unresolved risk,' but the summary does not establish materiality, only that storage-control documentation was inconsistent and follow-up was recommended.
The Actor's own packet concedes the support is weak and narrower than ideal, which suggests the evidentiary basis may be insufficient for a firm reject decision.

Quality-process gaps and questionnaire inconsistencies are explicitly described by policy as insufficient on their own to prove a reject-level control failure; the summary does not clearly show what additional admissible evidence elevates this to reject-level risk.
It is unclear from the admissible summary whether the storage-control issue remained unresolved at the actual time of decision, as opposed to merely requiring follow-up.
Because evidence access is limited to the Actor's summary, there is no direct way to test whether any unstated security-review information was indirectly relied on.
unsupported_claims: That the documented file, as summarized, clearly satisfies the policy requirement of a material unresolved risk supporting rejection.

That the combination of an inconsistency, an analyst follow-up recommendation, an informal quality process, and one late quality artifact is enough by itself to justify rejection rather than escalation or conditional hold.
Any implication that the record proves a reject-level control failure.
evidence_requests: Provide the exact admissible text from BPROC-033-D and BPROC-033-E showing the storage-controls inconsistency and confirming it was still unresolved when the decision was made.
Provide the exact language from BPROC-033-C showing approval was conditioned on resolving the storage-control issue, and whether non-resolution required rejection versus further escalation.
Provide the admissible record establishing why the unresolved storage-control issue was material rather than minor or administrative.
Provide the decision memo or equivalent admissible document showing the rejection rationale actually relied on these cited items and not on private security-review results.
Provide any admissible procurement policy or rubric mapping unresolved storage-control questions to a reject outcome.
decision_criteria: Rejecting the vendor is compliant only if admissible evidence shows a material unresolved due-diligence risk.
Quality-process gaps alone are insufficient for rejection under the stated policy.
Questionnaire inconsistencies alone are insufficient for rejection under the stated policy.
A recommendation for follow-up supports escalation, but does not by itself establish that rejection was required or justified.
No private security-review result may be cited or indirectly laundered unless formally logged.
